A.domain: Rational number arithmetic (fraction and mixed-number subtraction)

skills.name: Convert to improper fraction
skills.definition: Rewrite mixed numbers or whole numbers as equivalent fractions (often improper) with a specified denominator to enable fraction operations.
inclusion_criteria: Converting a mixed number a b/c into (ac+b)/c
Rewriting an integer n as an equivalent fraction n = (n·d)/d to match a denominator used in the problem
exclusion_criteria: Only finding a common denominator between two already-proper fractions (tag S02 instead)
Only simplifying/reducing a fraction after computation (tag S04 instead)

skills.name: Find common denominator
skills.definition: Determine a common (often least common) denominator and convert each fraction to an equivalent fraction with that denominator.
inclusion_criteria: Computing an LCM of denominators (explicitly or implicitly) to choose a common denominator
Scaling numerators/denominators to express both fractions over the same denominator
exclusion_criteria: Denominators are already equal and no conversion is needed (tag S03 instead)
Converting mixed/whole numbers to fractions without focusing on matching denominators (tag S01 instead)

skills.name: Subtract rational numbers
skills.definition: Compute the difference of two rational numbers once they are expressed in compatible form (same denominator or separated whole/fractional parts).
inclusion_criteria: Subtracting numerators over a common denominator (a/b − c/b = (a−c)/b)
Subtracting by combining whole-part and fractional-part differences in mixed numbers
Producing 0 or 1 from fraction subtraction (e.g., 2/3−2/3, 8/8=1)
exclusion_criteria: Steps that only set up equivalent fractions (tag S01 or S02 instead)
Steps that only reduce/simplify the final fraction (tag S04 instead)

skills.name: Simplify and format result
skills.definition: Reduce a fraction to lowest terms and/or express an improper fraction as a mixed number or integer when appropriate.
inclusion_criteria: Reducing a fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by a common factor
Stating that a fraction is already in lowest terms
Converting an improper fraction to a mixed number or to an integer (e.g., 3/3=1)
exclusion_criteria: Any conversion done primarily to enable subtraction (tag S01 or S02 instead)
The subtraction computation itself (tag S03 instead)

B.domain: Rational number arithmetic (fraction and mixed-number subtraction)

skills.name: Convert to equivalent fractions
skills.definition: Rewrite a fraction or whole number as an equivalent fraction with a specified denominator to enable subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Converting a fraction to an equivalent fraction by multiplying numerator and denominator (e.g., 5/3 = 20/12)
Rewriting an integer as a fraction with a chosen denominator (e.g., 2 = 16/8 or 3 = 15/5)
exclusion_criteria: Converting mixed numbers to improper fractions (tag S02 instead)
Reducing/simplifying a fraction to lowest terms (tag S04 instead)
Performing the subtraction operation itself once denominators match (tag S03 instead)

skills.name: Convert mixed to improper
skills.definition: Transform a mixed number (including nonstandard forms like 1 + 5/3) into an improper fraction by combining the whole and fractional parts.
inclusion_criteria: Using (whole×denominator + numerator)/denominator to convert a mixed number to an improper fraction
Interpreting and converting nonstandard mixed expressions where the fractional part exceeds 1 (e.g., 1 4/3 = 1 + 4/3 = 7/3)
exclusion_criteria: Only rewriting an integer as a fraction with a given denominator (tag S01 instead)
Subtracting whole and fractional parts directly without converting to improper fractions (tag S03 instead)

skills.name: Subtract rational numbers
skills.definition: Compute the difference of two rational numbers by subtracting numerators when denominators match (including decomposing mixed numbers into whole and fractional parts).
inclusion_criteria: Subtracting fractions with the same denominator by subtracting numerators
Subtracting after converting to a common denominator
Subtracting mixed numbers by separating whole and fractional parts (when no borrowing is needed in these items)
exclusion_criteria: Finding/creating a common denominator or equivalent fractions (tag S01 instead)
Converting mixed numbers to improper fractions (tag S02 instead)
Reducing the final fraction to lowest terms or converting improper to mixed as a simplification step (tag S04 instead)

skills.name: Simplify and format result
skills.definition: Express the computed result in an accepted simplest form by reducing fractions and/or converting between improper fractions, mixed numbers, and integers.
inclusion_criteria: Reducing a fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by a common factor
Recognizing and writing a result as an integer (e.g., 8/8 = 1 or 0/3 = 0)
Converting an improper fraction to a mixed number (or stating an equivalent mixed-number form)
exclusion_criteria: Creating equivalent fractions to match denominators before subtraction (tag S01 instead)
The subtraction computation step itself (tag S03 instead)

C.domain: Arithmetic with fractions and mixed numbers (subtraction, equivalence, simplification)

skills.name: Convert mixed/whole to fraction
skills.definition: Rewrite mixed numbers and whole numbers as equivalent improper fractions (or as fractions with a specified denominator) to enable fraction operations.
inclusion_criteria: Converting a mixed number a b/c into (ac+b)/c
Rewriting an integer n as n/1 or as an equivalent fraction with a target denominator (e.g., 3 = 15/5)
exclusion_criteria: Only finding a common denominator between two already-proper fractions (tag S02 instead)
Only reducing/simplifying a fraction after computation (tag S04 instead)

skills.name: Find common denominator
skills.definition: Determine a common denominator (often via LCM) and convert each fraction to an equivalent fraction with that denominator.
inclusion_criteria: Computing/choosing a common denominator such as 12, 8, 18, 24
Using LCM explicitly to select the denominator
Scaling numerators/denominators to create equivalent fractions with the common denominator
exclusion_criteria: Denominators are already equal and no conversion is needed (tag S03 instead)
Only converting mixed/whole numbers to improper fractions without aligning denominators (tag S01 instead)

skills.name: Subtract rational numbers
skills.definition: Compute the subtraction once numbers are in compatible forms (same denominator or separated whole/fraction parts), producing the raw difference.
inclusion_criteria: Subtracting numerators over a common denominator (e.g., 20/12 − 9/12)
Subtracting when denominators are already the same (e.g., (6−4)/7)
Subtracting by decomposing mixed numbers into whole-part and fractional-part differences
exclusion_criteria: Steps whose main purpose is to create equivalent fractions with a common denominator (tag S02 instead)
Steps whose main purpose is to simplify/reduce or convert the final form (tag S04 instead)

skills.name: Simplify and format result
skills.definition: Reduce a fraction to lowest terms and/or express an equivalent final form (integer or mixed number) consistent with the computed value.
inclusion_criteria: Reducing a fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by a common factor
Recognizing and rewriting results like 0/3 as 0 or 8/8 as 1
Converting an improper fraction to a mixed number (or stating an equivalent mixed-number form)
exclusion_criteria: Computing the subtraction itself (tag S03 instead)
Converting inputs (mixed/whole) before subtraction (tag S01 instead)
